## Idea
**Title:** Per-User Coupon Redemption Limits
**Complexity:** small

## Description
The Coupon entity has validity dates and a status field, but no per-user redemption limit. A single user could redeem the same coupon multiple times across different orders. This feature: (1) adds a `max_uses_per_user` field to the Coupon entity (defaulting to 1); (2) tracks how many times each user has redeemed each coupon; (3) during coupon validation at checkout, rejects the coupon if the user has already hit their limit; (4) returns a clear message like "You have already used this coupon" so the patient understands why it was rejected.

## Rationale
A basic coupon system gap that enables abuse. The Coupon entity has `valid_start`/`valid_end` and `status` but no redemption tracking. Without per-user limits, promotional coupons (especially high-value ones) can be exploited, undermining the coupon system's business purpose.

## Idea
**Title:** Drug Review Moderation Queue in Admin Backend
**Complexity:** medium

## Description
The DrugReview entity allows patients to submit reviews (rating, content, images), but there is no moderation workflow. Inappropriate, fraudulent, or medically misleading reviews could be displayed immediately. This feature: (1) adds a moderation status to drug reviews (pending/approved/rejected); (2) new reviews default to "pending" and are hidden from public drug pages until approved; (3) the admin backend gets a review moderation list view with approve/reject actions and a rejection reason field; (4) patient-facing drug detail pages only show "approved" reviews, with a count of total approved reviews.

## Rationale
For a pharmacy platform, unmoderated reviews carry medical risk — a fake positive review could mislead patients about drug efficacy or safety. The admin backend already has 24+ controllers for operational management; a review moderation queue is a natural and necessary addition to the content safety layer.

---

## Idea
**Title:** Cart-Level Drug Interaction Warnings
**Complexity:** small

## Description
The AIAssistantController already supports drug interaction checking via the Baichuan LLM, but it requires the patient to proactively ask. This feature brings interaction checking into the cart flow: (1) when the cart is validated (existing `/v1/cart/validate` endpoint) or when items are added, the system automatically checks for known interactions among all drugs currently in the cart; (2) if potential interactions are detected, the patient sees a warning banner listing the drug pairs and a brief risk summary, with a link to the AI assistant for a deeper analysis; (3) the warning is non-blocking — the patient can acknowledge and proceed, preserving autonomy while ensuring informed consent.

## Rationale
This leverages the existing AI integration in a high-impact, low-friction way. Multi-drug purchases are common, and patients often don't think to ask about interactions. The AI integration is already built; this just connects it to the cart validation pipeline where it can prevent real harm.

---

## Idea
**Title:** Patient-Side Doctor Appointment Booking Flow
**Complexity:** medium

## Description
The DoctorSchedule entity and DoctorController exist, but the patient-side booking flow appears incomplete — patients can view doctor schedules but there is no clear endpoint or UI flow to book a specific time slot for a consultation. This feature: (1) adds a booking endpoint where a patient selects a doctor, date, and time slot; (2) atomically increments `booked_count` on the DoctorSchedule and prevents overbooking when `booked_count >= max_patients`; (3) creates a Consultation record in "pending" status linked to the chosen schedule; (4) returns a booking confirmation with the consultation ID so the patient can proceed to the consultation room.

## Rationale
The data model has all the pieces — DoctorSchedule with max_patients/booked_count, Consultation with status workflow — but the actual booking transaction that ties them together is missing. Without it, the consultation flow is fragmented: patients can see doctors and their schedules but can't initiate a consultation from that context.

## Idea
**Title:** Stock Reservation During Checkout to Prevent Overselling
**Complexity:** medium

## Description
When a patient proceeds to checkout, the current system validates cart items but does not reserve inventory. This creates a race condition where two patients could simultaneously purchase the last unit of a drug. This feature introduces a temporary stock hold: (1) at checkout initiation, the requested quantities are reserved (reducing available stock) with a short TTL; (2) if payment succeeds, the reservation becomes permanent; (3) if payment times out or the user abandons checkout, the reservation is released; (4) the drug listing shows "X in stock (Y reserved)" to set accurate expectations.

## Rationale
A critical e-commerce integrity gap. The Drug entity tracks `stock` and `sales` fields, and the cart has a `validate` endpoint, but there is no atomic reservation step between validation and order creation. This is especially important for pharmacy items where stock-outs have health implications.

---

## Idea
**Title:** Prescription Refill Request
**Complexity:** medium

## Description
Patients with an approved, fulfilled prescription can request a refill without re-uploading the original prescription document — if the prescribing doctor indicated the prescription is refillable and refills remain. The patient sees a "Request Refill" button on any eligible past prescription. The request creates a new order entry linked to the original prescription, skipping the document upload step but still requiring prescription re-verification if the original has expired. The system tracks remaining refill count and decrements it on each successful refill order.

## Rationale
AGENTS.md describes a Prescription state machine but makes no mention of refills. Chronic disease patients — the most frequent pharmacy users — regularly need refills for ongoing medications. Forcing them to re-upload the same prescription every time creates unnecessary friction and may lead to treatment gaps.

## Idea
**Title:** Patient Health Profile for Personalized AI Diagnosis
**Complexity:** medium

## Description
Patients can optionally fill out a health profile including: age, gender, known allergies (drug and food), chronic conditions, current medications, and relevant medical history (surgeries, family history). During AI diagnosis sessions, the Baichuan prompt automatically includes relevant profile data so the AI can give more personalized and safer recommendations — for example, flagging that a suggested medicine conflicts with a known allergy. The profile is editable at any time and is shared with doctors during IM consultations (with patient consent per session). All health profile data is encrypted at rest per existing compliance requirements.

## Rationale
The AGENTS.md mentions real-name verification (realName/idCard) and AI diagnosis via Baichuan, but no mechanism to give the AI patient-specific context. Without it, every AI consultation starts from zero — the AI doesn't know the patient's allergies, conditions, or current medications. This is both a missed personalization opportunity and a safety risk.

---

## Idea
**Title:** Doctor Online Status & Consultation Request
**Complexity:** medium

## Description
Patients can see which certified doctors are currently online and available for IM consultation. The doctor list shows name, specialty, years of experience, and an online/offline status indicator. Patients can send a consultation request to an online doctor, which the doctor can accept or decline. Once accepted, a TIM chat session opens between them. If no doctor is online, the patient can leave a consultation request that notifies doctors when they come online. A simple queue prevents any single doctor from being overwhelmed with simultaneous requests.

## Rationale
AGENTS.md confirms Doctor entities exist with license verification and TIM IM integration, but there's no mention of how patients actually find and connect with available doctors. Without a presence/availability system, the doctor-patient IM channel is effectively unusable — patients would be messaging doctors who aren't there, and doctors would have no way to signal availability.

## Idea
**Title:** Admin Dashboard with Key Metrics
**Complexity:** medium

## Description
The admin backend gains a dashboard view showing key operational metrics: total orders today/this week, prescription review queue depth, revenue summary, top-selling medicines, new user registrations, and pending doctor certifications. Each metric card is clickable to drill into the relevant management view (e.g., tapping "12 prescriptions pending review" navigates to the prescription review queue). The dashboard loads with a simple date-range filter (today, this week, this month, custom).

## Rationale
AGENTS.md lists a full admin backend (Spring Boot + Vue 3 + Element Plus) but describes no dashboard or overview. Admin operators managing prescriptions, doctors, and orders need an at-a-glance view of what requires attention — otherwise they must navigate into each subsystem blindly to find pending work.

## Idea
**Title:** Medication Reminder System
**Complexity:** large

## Description
Patients can set medication reminders for any purchased prescription or OTC medicine. For each medicine, they configure: dosage (e.g., "1 tablet"), frequency (e.g., "twice daily"), time of day, and duration (e.g., "7 days"). The system sends in-app notification reminders at the scheduled times. A daily adherence checklist lets patients mark doses as taken, missed, or skipped. The adherence summary over the treatment period is visible in the patient's profile and can be shared with a consulting doctor via the IM channel. Reminders automatically deactivate after the treatment duration ends.

## Rationale
Medication non-adherence affects 50% of chronic disease patients and leads to poor health outcomes and preventable hospitalizations. For a pharmacy platform, reminders are a high-retention feature that directly connects the purchase (buying medicine) to the outcome (taking it correctly). AGENTS.md mentions no notification infrastructure — adding a focused, in-app notification system for reminders is a natural first step.

---
